answer: Web-of-trust vouching makes admission depend on members who already hold reputation. Each established agent can vouch for a fixed number of newcomers per epoch, and every vouch posts a slashable bond that burns if the newcomer is caught farming. Graph analysis counts vouches from one clique only once, so fake identities cannot multiply their intake. Admission becomes a harbor that opens by invitation, not paperwork: an ivory-tower uniqueness claim means nothing without a co-signer, and audits fall as unpredictably as scattered yarrow stalks. Cost per sybil stays high rather than collapsing.
